questions.question: The lead chromate which is toxic and carcinogenic, is used for the adulteration of _________ powder.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**turmeric.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Lead and chromium** are the two elements that make up** lead chromate.**
 
• It is a** yellow pigment** that can increase a **substance's brightness.**
 
• It is also **dangerous **and, when** consumed or inhaled** by people, acts as a **neurotoxin.**
 
• It** causes cognitive flaws.**
 
• Typically, lead chromate is used by manufacturers to **provide yellow and orange color** to **oils and paints.**
 
• **Turmeric** has been linked to **lead exposure **in numerous** Bangladeshi districts **where it is grown, according to study.
 
• Lead damages **children's neurodevelopment **and exposes **both adults and children **to heart and **brain diseases.​**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Food adulteration** refers to the practice of** lowering the quality of food** products by either

 
 
• introducing **hazardous substances** into them or
 
• removing** beneficial components** from them.
 
 
 
• **Sugar, glucose, and sugar syrup** are common adulterants in **honey.**
 
• **Vegetable oil, starch, and vanaspati** are frequently found as adulterants in **ghee.**
 
• **Brick powder and artificial colours** are frequent adulterants in** red chilli powder.**
 
• In **pulses, artificial colours** are frequently used as adulterants.
 
• **Pebble, broken grains and polish** are typical adulterants in **rice.**
 
• **Wax coating** is a typical **apple** adulterant.
 
• **Salt** is frequently contaminated with **chalk powder.**

questions.question: Starches found in bread, cereals and pasta are made up of long chains of _______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**glucose**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbohydrates: 

 
 
• **Carbohydrates, or carbs, are sugar molecules.**
 
• Along with proteins and fats, **carbohydrates **are one of the three main nutrients found in foods and drinks.
 
• **Your body breaks down carbohydrates into glucose.**
 
• Glucose, or blood sugar, is the main source of energy for your body's cells, tissues, and organs.
 
• **Carbohydrates **are found in a wide array of both healthy and unhealthy foods.
 
• Bread, beans, milk, popcorn, potatoes, cookies, spaghetti, soft drinks, corn, and cherry pie.
 
• The most common and abundant forms are sugars, fibres, and starches.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** 

 
• **Glycogen, starch and cellulose are polymers of Glucose.**
 
• **Polymers **are materials made of long, **repeating chains of molecules.**
 
• **Glycogen **serves as a form of energy storage in humans, animals, fungi, and bacteria.
 
• **Starch **is a polymer made by plants to store energy.
 
• **Cellulose **is the main substance that makes up the cell walls and fibers of plants.

questions.question: In alchemy, aqua fortis is the classical name of which chemical compound that is used chiefly in the manufacture of explosives and fertilisers, and in organic synthesis?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitric acid**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nitric acid (HNO₃), **also known as aqua fortis, derived from Latin for **"strong water," **is a potent and corrosive mineral acid renowned for its reactivity with various metals, including silver. It is colorless and fuming in nature.
 
• Primarily, nitric acid finds extensive application in the production of fertilizers and explosives.
 
• Approximately 80% of its usage is attributed to fertilizer production, with a minor portion allocated to explosive manufacturing.
 
• Additionally, nitric acid is referred to as spirit of niter. Notably, accidental exposure to nitric acid can pose severe health risks, and in some cases, it can be fatal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Formic acid**, with the chemical formula HCOOH and molecular structure H−C−O−H, is recognized as the simplest carboxylic acid. It occurs naturally in certain ant species and is found in the venom of bee and ant stings.
 
• **Chloric acid,** represented by the chemical formula HClO₃, is a colorless liquid known for its strong acidic and oxidizing properties. It serves as a precursor to chlorate salts.
 
• **Hydrobromic acid** presents as a colorless to light yellow liquid characterized by its highly acidic and corrosive nature. It is classified as a strong mineral acid, formed by dissolving hydrogen bromide in water.

questions.question: Which element of the boron family has a high boiling point, making it ideal for recording temperatures that would vaporise a thermometer?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**Gallium**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **​Gallium (Ga)** is a member of the boron family, positioned in **Group 13 of the Periodic Table**, with an **atomic number of 31 **and a relative **atomic mass of 69.723**.
 
• Gallium possesses a notably high boiling point of around** 2200°C **(3992°F), rendering it suitable for applications requiring the measurement of extreme temperatures that would vaporize conventional thermometers.
 
• Gallium finds various applications:
 
 
• **Specialized Thermometers: **Gallium is utilized in specialized thermometers engineered for high temperatures. These gallium thermometers provide a safe and accurate alternative to traditional mercury thermometers, which pose hazards due to mercury toxicity.
 
• **Semiconductor Production:** Gallium is a crucial constituent in semiconductor manufacturing. Gallium arsenide (GaAs) is employed to fabricate high-frequency electronic devices like microwave transistors and light-emitting diodes (LEDs).
 
• **Alloying Agent: **Gallium is alloyed with other metals to produce materials with specific properties. For instance, gallium-indium-tin alloys are utilized in liquid metal cooling systems for electronics, offering efficient heat transfer capabilities.
 
• **Nuclear Medicine:** Gallium-67, a radioactive isotope of gallium, plays a vital role in nuclear medicine for diagnostic imaging purposes. It is utilized to detect and diagnose certain diseases, aiding in medical diagnostics and treatment planning.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Thallium **belongs to the boron family, specifically Group 13, in the periodic table, with an atomic number of 81. Due to its relatively low boiling point, thallium is not suitable for measuring high temperatures that would cause a thermometer to vaporize.
 
• **Aluminium** is another member of the boron family, with an atomic number of 13. While aluminium has a moderate boiling point, it is not exceptionally high, making it unsuitable for recording extremely high temperatures.
 
• **Indium** is also part of the boron family, with an atomic number of 49. Compared to gallium, indium has a lower boiling point, rendering it less suitable for applications requiring the measurement of high temperatures.

questions.question: Compounds with exactly two double carbon–carbon bonds are known as ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Dienes.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **A molecule called diene **has** two double bonds between its carbon** atoms and is **unsaturated.**
 
• **Diene** is employed in industry as a** complex polymer's monomer constituent.** 
 
• It is also used in **Organic Synthesis.**
 
• Dienes are divided into** three groups** based on where the** double bond is located **relative to the rest of the molecule:
 
 
• A **cumulated diene** is one that has **two consecutive double bonds** on nearby Carbon atoms. They go by the name** Allene too.**
 
• A **conjugated diene** is a compound with **two conjugated double bonds** that are spaced apart by just** one bond.**
 
• **Two double bonds** that are spaced apart by** two or more double bond**s make up an** isolated diene.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Terpenes:**

 
 
• Terpenes are a group of **organic compounds** with the formula** (C₅H₈)n,** where **n is greater than 1. **
 
 
 
• **Alkyne:**
 
 
• Alkynes are hydrocarbons that have **triple bonds between carbon atoms.**
 
• When it comes to** molecules with one triple bond**, their usual formula is **CₙH₂ₙ₋₂ (and no rings).**

questions.question: Which of the following scientists grouped the elements into triads?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Johann Wolfgang Dobereiner**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Johann Wolfgang Döbereiner, a German chemist,** was one of the first to classify elements based on their similar properties.
 
• In 1829, **he observed that certain groups of three elements had similar chemical properties **and
 
 
• that the atomic mass of the middle element was roughly the average of the other two.
 
 
 
• These **groups of three elements became known as "Döbereiner’s Triads."**
 
• **For example**:
 
 
• Lithium, Sodium, Potassium: In this triad, sodium’s atomic mass is the average of lithium and potassium.
 
• Chlorine, Bromine, Iodine: These elements also formed a triad with similar chemical behavior.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **John Newlands**

 
 
• **Newlands proposed the Law of Octaves**, where he arranged elements in increasing order of atomic mass and noticed that every eighth element had similar properties.
 
• His **work was an important step toward the development of the modern periodic table,** but it was initially criticized for not being applicable to all elements.
 
• His classification system was later recognized as a precursor to Mendeleev’s work.
 
 
 
• **Henry Moseley**
 
 
• Moseley **established the concept of atomic numb**er, which is the number of protons in the nucleus of an atom.
 
• His work showed that elements are better arranged by increasing atomic number rather than atomic mass, leading to a more accurate periodic table.
 
• **His research resolved inconsistencies in Mendeleev’s periodic table.**
 
 
 
• **Dmitri Mendeleev**
 
 
• Mendeleev is **credited with creating the first widely recognized periodic table in 1869.**
 
• He **arranged elements by increasing atomic mass **and left gaps for undiscovered elements, predicting their properties with great accuracy.
 
• Mendeleev’s periodic law laid the groundwork for modern chemistry.

questions.question: In which year did Albert Einstein predict a new state of matter, the Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC), based on a quantum formulation by the Indian physicist Satyendra Nath Bose?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__1924.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Albert Einstein's **prediction of the **Bose-Einstein condensate (BEC) in 1924** was based on the quantum formulations put forth by Indian physicist **Satyendra Nath Bose**.
 
• This groundbreaking state of matter, often referred to as the** fifth state of matter,** was a result of Bose's foundational work on quantum mechanics in the early 1920s.
 
• Bose's contributions included the development of Bose-Einstein statistics and the theoretical framework for the BEC.
 
• The first** "pure" **BEC was subsequently created by Eric Cornell, Carl Wieman, and their colleagues at JILA on June 5, 1995.
 
• In a notable advancement, the **Cold Atom Laboratory experiment **conducted aboard the International Space Station achieved the creation of a BEC consisting of rubidium atoms in June 2020.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Satyendra Nath Bose, **an Indian mathematician and physicist, was highly regarded for his contributions to theoretical physics, particularly in the field of quantum mechanics during the early 1920s.
 
• His notable achievements include laying the groundwork for Bose-Einstein statistics and formulating the theory of the Bose-Einstein condensate.
 
• Recognized for his scholarly pursuits, Bose was elected as a Fellow of the Royal Society.
 
• In acknowledgment of his outstanding contributions to science, the Government of India conferred upon him the Padma Vibhushan, the nation's second highest civilian award, in 1954.

questions.question: What is the ratio by mass of nitrogen and hydrogen in ammonia?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**14 **____**∶ 3**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Ammonia (NH3)**

__
 
• The law of constant composition states that a given chemical compound always contains its component elements in a fixed ratio (by mass) and does not depend on its source and method of preparation.
 
• Nitrogen makes up about 14/17 of the mass of any sample of pure Ammonia, while Hydrogen makes up the remaining 3/17 of the mass. (Atomic weight of nitrogen is 14 and that of hydrogen is 1)
 
• That is Ammonia, **Nitrogen, and Hydrogen are always present in the ratio 14:3 by mass.**
 
• 1 atom of Nitrogen is always combined with 3 atoms of Hydrogen.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Atomic mass is the quantity of matter contained in an atom of an element. 
 
• It is expressed as a multiple of one-twelfth the mass of the carbon-12 atom.
 
• Mass ratio, often called "per cent composition by mass," is the proportion of a particular molecule that consists of each of that molecule's constituent elements.

questions.question: Carbon dating means __________.

options.text: a method to determine the density of fissile material
a method of calculating the remains of sulphur and nitrogen in hard rock
a method of calculating the age of very old objects by measuring the amounts of different forms of carbon in them
a method of determination of weight of a very old rock

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__a method of calculating the age of very old objects by measuring the amounts of different forms of carbon in them__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Carbon dating:

 
 
• Carbon dating is a technique used to determine the approximate age of once-living materials.
 
• It is also referred to as Radiocarbon dating.
 
• Radiocarbon dating is a method of estimating the age of an artefact or biological vestige based on the relative amount of various isotopes of carbon present in a sample.
 
• Age can be estimated by measuring the amount of carbon-14 present in the sample and comparing this against an internationally used reference standard.
 
• Radiocarbon decays slowly in a living organism but once the organism dies, it ceases to absorb Carbon-14 so that the amount of the radiocarbon in the tissues steadily decreases.
 
• Because carbon-14 decays at a constant rate, an estimate of the date at which an organism dies can be made by measuring the amount of its residual radiocarbon.
 
• It was developed in the late 1940s by Williard Libby.
 
• Carbon dating is one of the most effective tools in the archaeologist's kit.
 
• It is a vital part of the investigation and preservation of our past.
 
• The oldest dates that can be reliably measured by this process date to approximately 50,000 years.
 
• Histories of archaeology often refer to its impact as the "radiocarbon revolution".
 
• Radiocarbon dating has allowed key transitions in prehistory to be dated, such as the end of the last Ice Age, and the beginning of the Neolithic and Bronze Age in different regions.
 
 

Thus, we can say that Carbon dating is **a method of calculating the age of very old objects by measuring the amounts of different forms of carbon in them.**__

• **John Dalton**, in his **atomic theory**, proposed a system of symbols to represent various chemical elements.
 
• He used simple shapes and patterns, often circles, to illustrate atoms of different elements.

• **Element symbols **for **chemical elements **normally consist of **one or two letters **from the **Latin alphabet **and are written with the **first letter capitalised**.
 
• **A chemical symbol **is a **one- or two-letter **designation of **an element**.

• Some examples of **chemical symbols **are **O for oxygen**, **Zn for zinc**, **H for hydrogen, **and **Fe for iron**.

questions.question: From the given options, choose the one which is NOT a product of the decomposition reaction of Lead nitrate.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Nitrogen**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nitrogen** is not produced as a** direct product of the decomposition reaction of lead nitrate. **
 
• When** lead nitrate **is heated, it undergoes decomposition into **lead oxide, nitrogen dioxide, and oxygen**. 
 
• The chemical equation representing this reaction is:
 
 
• **2Pb(NO₃)₂(s) → 2PbO(s) + 4NO₂(g) + O₂(g)**
 
 
 
• In this reaction, lead nitrate decomposes to form solid lead oxide and gases nitrogen dioxide and oxygen. 
 
• The **lead oxide** remains in solid form, while the** nitrogen dioxide and oxygen **are released as gases.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A decomposition reaction**, also referred to as chemical breakdown, is a type of chemical reaction in which a single reactant molecule breaks down into two or more products.
 
• The general form of a decomposition reaction is represented as AB → A + B, where AB denotes the parent molecule or reactant.
 
• Decomposition reactions typically necessitate an input of energy, which can be provided in the form of heat, light, or electricity. Higher temperatures often facilitate the decomposition process, accelerating the rate of reaction.
 
• Depending on the specific reaction conditions, the overall process can either absorb heat from the surroundings (endothermic) or release heat to the surroundings (exothermic).

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a food preservative?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Aqua regia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Aqua regia,** a potent liquid, is characterized by its corrosive, acidic, and oxidative properties, resulting from a blend of hydrochloric acid and nitric acid.
 
• Its chemical formula, HNO₃+3 HCl, reflects the mixture with a standard ratio of three parts hydrochloric acid to one part nitric acid. Initially, aqua regia appears fuming and colorless, but it swiftly transforms into hues of yellow, orange, or red upon preparation.
 
• This solution finds widespread application in metallurgy, where it effectively dissolves metals such as gold and platinum, either for analytical purposes or to eliminate trace contaminants.
 
• Furthermore, aqua regia serves as a crucial agent in glassware cleaning procedures and plays a pivotal role in gold refining processes.
 
• The name "aqua regia" originates from the Latin term "royal water," denoting its unique ability to dissolve noble metals like gold and platinum, traditionally associated with royalty. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Food preservatives **play a crucial role in preventing food spoilage caused by microbial growth, thereby extending the shelf life of various food products and ensuring their safety.
 
• Commonly used food preservatives include sugar, table salt, vegetable oil, and sodium benzoate.
 
• Salt, for instance, is employed to inhibit microbial growth in vegetables and meats, effectively preserving their freshness.
 
• Additionally, sorbic acid and propanoic acid salts are widely utilized as preservatives, further enhancing the stability and safety of food products.
 
• These preservatives help to control the growth of bacteria and other microorganisms, thereby maintaining the quality and integrity of the food.
